precepts.text: By their secret plots and popular persuasions and commotions they hindered the finishing of the building.
precepts.point: Israelites with a house-servant spirit want to find the enemy a place in Israel's salvation. Israel will build alone.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
“Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel”, these heathen, placed in the land in the time of Assyria, came and said, “Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do”. We want to serve God, we want to be around you, we want to cleave. But at that time we were back from exile and not ruling; we were under Persian subjugation.

1 Esdras gives the answer: “It is not for us and you to build together an house unto the Lord our God. We ourselves alone will build unto the Lord of Israel”. We ourselves alone. We don't need your help. Our forefathers understood that in captivity solidarity and unity were paramount. Yet today, as this truth grows and is harder to blackball, there are Israelites with a house negro spirit trying to find a place in our salvation for our enemies, whose heaven is our hell. That is post-traumatic slave disorder, and it is pushing the same agenda into the truth.

Because they were told no, “the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building”. You know how Esau gets when he is told no: he turns into a different beast. It is the same when black folks built for themselves: Black Wall Street, Rosewood, Tulsa, Seneca Village, Black Bottom in Detroit, Lake Lanier. Whenever we build, they come along wanting in, and then destroy it.

“And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building”. Secret plots are the laws they passed: redlining, blackballing, Jim Crow, systematic laws to make sure black folks don't thrive again, because left to ourselves we rebuild. Segregation was the best thing for us; integration in captivity destroyed us. Popular persuasions today are Christianity, social media, politics, philosophies, New Year's Eve, Christmas, Halloween, Easter, Islam, money, podcasters and content creators.

“so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.” Their plan was never to join us. If they really believed in helping, why go through all this to stop the building? Their plan was to join, infiltrate and destroy from the inside, like the Black Panthers: first the feminist and lesbian black women were let in, and a feminist-minded black woman is the white man with breasts and melanin, the white man's drone; then the white folks came in, and it was a wrap. Martin King found at the end that he had integrated his people into a burning house. That is why our fathers said, we ourselves alone will build.

The pattern holds in our history: in exile in Europe we taught Esau our laws, and he destroyed us and became us; in Africa we taught the Arab, and he enslaved us. When you are in exile, you do not share your wisdom with the nations. The time is to keep the commandments of God and the faith of his Son, gain favour with our God, and get out of this condition, then deal with the nations after that.

precepts.text: There have been mighty kings over Jerusalem which ruled over all countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom was paid unto them.
precepts.point: Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. The kings failed when they forsook the law, and their power was given to a strange nation; that is why the kings of the scriptures are not known as black kings today. When the King of kings returns He restores the crowns, and He sets crowns on the heads of the great multitude on mount Sion.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“There have been mighty kings also over Jerusalem, which have ruled over all countries beyond the river; and toll, tribute, and custom, was paid unto them.”

That is “kings shall come out of thy loins” fulfilled. Israel once had mighty kings who ruled over countries beyond the river, and tribute and custom were paid unto them. They failed when they forsook the law and their power was given to a strange nation, but the mighty kings over Jerusalem came out of Israel's loins.

precepts.text: The adversaries said, Let us build with you, for we seek your God; the fathers answered, Ye have nothing to do with us, but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel.
precepts.point: He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God. Israel should walk confident, special, and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else; repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
The other nations knew whose God He was. “Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel”, they came to Zerubbabel and the chief of the fathers and said, “Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do”.

The answer: “Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God; but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel”. Zerubbabel, Jeshua and the chief of the fathers knew that the Lord dwells among the children of Israel and is their God, and no one else's.

That is the mindset for these last days. Israel does not need the other nations' assistance; the nation rebuilds one another spiritually, ourselves together, while awaiting Christ's return to restore the kingdom. Repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High, who belongs to no one else.

precepts.text: The king of Assyria brought men from Babylon and other cities and placed them in Samaria instead of Israel.
precepts.point: These were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, not true worshippers but taught only to appease the God of the land.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
The adversaries who came to Zerubbabel say they have sacrificed to the God of Israel “since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.” Second Kings tells who they were: “the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel: and they possessed Samaria, and dwelt in the cities thereof.”

So these were not Israel. They were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land and set in Samaria in the place of the children of Israel. When they said “we seek your God, as ye do”, they were strangers the Assyrian had planted there, and that is why they were the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin and not brethren building with them.

precepts.text: Not fearing the Lord, they were slain by lions, and they reported they knew not the manner of the God of the land.
precepts.point: These were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, not true worshippers but taught only to appease the God of the land.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
When those nations first dwelt in Samaria “they feared not the Lord: therefore the Lord sent lions among them, which slew some of them.” They sent word to the king of Assyria that “The nations which thou hast removed, and placed in the cities of Samaria, know not the manner of the God of the land: therefore he hath sent lions among them, and, behold, they slay them, because they know not the manner of the God of the land.”

That is the beginning of their sacrificing “unto him since the days of Esar–haddon.” They did not come to the God of Israel as true worshippers; they were being killed by lions and wanted to appease the God of the land. That is the worship the adversaries were offering to bring into the house of the Lord.

precepts.text: A captive priest was sent back to teach them how to fear the Lord, yet every nation still made gods of their own.
precepts.point: These were peoples the king of Assyria had brought into the land, not true worshippers but taught only to appease the God of the land.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
The king of Assyria answered the lions by sending a captive back: “Carry thither one of the priests whom ye brought from thence; and let them go and dwell there, and let him teach them the manner of the God of the land.” So “one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria came and dwelt in Beth–el, and taught them how they should fear the Lord.”

They were taught only enough to appease the God of the land, and every nation still made gods of their own. So when they told Zerubbabel and the chief of the fathers, “we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur”, that was the whole of it: strangers taught by a captive priest to fear the Lord alongside their own gods. That is why Judah and Benjamin could not let them build the temple unto the Lord God of Israel with them.

precepts.text: The building of the temple in Jerusalem was hindered and ceased until the second year of Darius.
precepts.point: The work of the house of God ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia. The same account, with a troop of horsemen halting the work, is told in 1 Esdras.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

precepts.why:
The same account is told in 1 Esdras. When king Artexerxes' letters were read, “Rathumus, and Semellius the scribe, and the rest that were in commission with them”, the Rehum and Shimshai of Ezra 4, went “in haste toward Jerusalem with a troop of horsemen and a multitude of people in battle array, began to hinder the builders; and the building of the temple in Jerusalem ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.”

This shows what “by force and power” meant: a troop of horsemen and a multitude in battle array sent against the builders. Both books end the same way: the work of the house of God ceased, and it stayed ceased until the second year of the reign of Darius.

precepts.text: The people of the land weakened the hands of Judah, troubled them in building, and hired counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose, the same hindering spirit against the rebuilding.
precepts.point: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, hear of it, it grieves them exceedingly that a man has come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

precepts.why:
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard that a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, it grieved them exceedingly. This is the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before: “Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building, And hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.”

The people of the land weakened Judah's hands, troubled them in building, and hired counsellors against them to frustrate their purpose, and kept it up from Cyrus to Darius. That same hindering spirit against the rebuilding met Nehemiah the moment he arrived with the king's letters and his escort of captains and horsemen.

precepts.text: The enemies wrote to the king that if the rebellious city were built and the walls set up, the Jews would no more pay toll, tribute, and custom, and so damage the revenue of kings, the same mindset that fears Israel's rebuilding.
precepts.point: When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, hear of it, it grieves them exceedingly that a man has come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, the same opposition seen when the nation tried to rebuild before.

note.label: Nehemiah 2: The King Sends Nehemiah to Rebuild

precepts.why:
The enemies in Ezra's day wrote to the king: “Be it known unto the king, that the Jews which came up from thee to us are come unto Jerusalem, building the rebellious and the bad city, and have set up the walls thereof, and joined the foundations. Be it known now unto the king, that, if this city be builded, and the walls set up again, then will they not pay toll, tribute, and custom, and so thou shalt endamage the revenue of the kings.”

They called Jerusalem the rebellious and the bad city, and their argument was money: if the walls go up, the Jews will no more pay toll, tribute and custom, and the revenue of kings will suffer. That is the same mindset that fears Israel's rebuilding. Sanballat and Tobiah were grieved exceedingly for the same reason: a man had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel, and Israel restored is a loss to those who profit from Israel down.
